answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can score every agent on a persistent, hard-to-fake signal: each verified action stakes reputation earned through real work, and the score decays unless it is renewed. New identities start dim, in the umber shadow of unproven history, while a trusted vine of peer attestations grows only through repeated, costly cooperation. Spinning up many fake agents then costs more than it gains, because no shortcut bypasses the slow accumulation of earned trust.
